Microneedling, aka collagen induction therapy: this procedure has the best healing and recovery time.  It works by pricking the skin's surface with small sterilized needles. This jumpstarts collagen and elastin production, which improves the skin's texture, tone, and firmness.  It is used to treat sun damage, burns, dark spots, and large pores and works on most skin tones; 
Microdermabrasion is a minimally invasive technique used to make your skin look smoother and healthier by "sanding" the top layers of the skin.  It is a quick procedure with no downtime, which may require multiple sessions to get desired results;  
CO2 laser treatments remove surface skin cells and simultaneously penetrate deeper into the skin to stimulate new collagen production.  There are several types of CO2 lasers so see your dermatologist for guidance. This treatment typically requires general anesthesia, a downtime of at least 2 weeks, and is often recommended for fair or light skin tones; and 
"Fractional CO2 laser resurfacing" is a newer procedure using a partial light beam that targets only a fraction of the skin.  It prevents damage to the skin's top layer, delivering maximum results with minimal pain and recovery time. It is not recommended for those with darker skin tones due to risk of hyperpigmentation.
